metadata.register: Conversational-Balanced, first-person, honest and straightforward — not the house Teardown/am_onyx register cli-explainer defaults to. Matches the af_bella / @HumanitariansAI precedent set on this user's other reels.
metadata.note: User asked for a 'CLI Explainer' by name. Built on the cli-explainer skill's REQUIRED story spine (B00 cold open -> PROBLEM -> ASK -> CODE -> OUTPUT -> CHANGE -> CODE -> OUTPUT -> SUMMARY -> NEXT STEPS -> OUTRO, real code shown via ClaudeCodeBeat, one required revision cycle) but with two disclosed substitutions: (1) voice/branding — af_bella + @HumanitariansAI instead of the skill's default Teardown/am_onyx/@NikBearBrown, per explicit user request for a woman's voice and matching this user's other two reels; (2) render pipeline — the skill's documented `vox_run.sh`/`vox_compile.py`/`type_check.py` do not exist in this toolkit install (verified: not found anywhere under runtime/scripts or runtime/qc); rendered instead through the same run.sh/compile.py/static_scene_check.py/manim_layout_audit.py/final_frame_check.py pipeline used successfully on this user's other three reels this session. The CLI loop's 'build' is real: weekly_recap_v1.py and weekly_recap_v2.py are genuine Python scripts, both actually run (not invented) to capture the CODE/OUTPUT beats' real source and output. v1 is a flat, undifferentiated list of the week's three items; v2 splits them into DONE THIS WEEK vs STARTING NEXT WEEK -- a real structural revision, not a cosmetic one, which doubles as the user's own stated concern (their revision-prompt template #5 asked for exactly this separation) already resolved in the initial cut. CORRECTED KICKOFF (per user request, replaces the original content wholesale): the week's three items are now (1) writing/publishing the AI-nonprofit-marketing article with real research behind it, (2) producing the accompanying Brutalist video for that article (this session's own ai-nonprofit-marketing build, 16:9 + 9:16), and (3) speaking engagements — a confirmed guest-speaker slot at Suffolk University this coming Wednesday with Yatra, plus two team meetings already attended this week. The fashion-sustainability framing from the original build is fully replaced, not layered on top of. weekly_recap_v1.py/v2.py, scenes.py's three card visuals (article/research, video-production, Suffolk-talk), and every topic-specific narration line were rewritten to match; the bookend beats (B00 intro, B01 problem, B09 handoff, B10 outro) needed no change since they were already generic. The article's publication venue was not specified by the user, so the script/narration say 'published this week' rather than inventing a platform name — see FACTCHECK.md.

beats.narration_text: Most weekly updates are a highlight reel — the wins, dressed up. I wanted something closer to a real log: what actually got done, kept separate from what's just getting started.

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL generated code, trimmed to what teaches; weekly_recap_v1.py was really run
beats.narration_text: Here's what it wrote — a flat list, three entries, no ranking, no spin. Just: published this, produced this, and what's coming up.

props.title: weekly_recap_v1.py
props.code:
WEEK = [
    {"item": "Published the AI nonprofit marketing article",
     "where": "published this week"},
    {"item": "Produced the accompanying video (16:9 + 9:16)",
     "where": "brutalist.art"},
    {"item": "Suffolk University talk, with Yatra",
     "where": "this Wednesday"},
]

def log():
    for entry in WEEK:
        print(f"- {entry['item']}  ({entry['where']})")

beats.role_note: OPEN vox slot -> Manim video; the real weekly_recap_v1.py output, visualized as three same-weight cards
beats.narration_text: Run it, and here's the week: the nonprofit marketing article, with real research behind it. The video that goes with it, actually produced — both formats. And a talk at Suffolk University, coming up with Yatra. All three, same weight, no sense of what's finished and what's just beginning.
beats.visual_intent: Manim: three cards in a flat row — an article/research card, a video-production icon card labeled 16:9 + 9:16, a Suffolk University talk card — all the same visual weight, undifferentiated

beats.narration_text: That's the problem, though — a flat list treats 'I published this' the same as 'I'm speaking on Wednesday.' So: revise it. Split what's actually finished from what's just starting.

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the revised code; weekly_recap_v2.py was really run
beats.narration_text: Same week, same three items — now in two lists. Done: the article, the video. Next: Suffolk University, this Wednesday.

props.title: weekly_recap_v2.py
props.code:
DONE = [
    {"item": "Published the AI nonprofit marketing article",
     "where": "published this week"},
    {"item": "Produced the accompanying video (16:9 + 9:16)",
     "where": "brutalist.art"},
]

NEXT = [
    {"item": "Suffolk University talk, with Yatra",
     "where": "this Wednesday"},
]

def log():
    print("DONE THIS WEEK")
    ...
    print("STARTING NEXT WEEK")
    ...

beats.role_note: OPEN vox slot -> Manim video; the real weekly_recap_v2.py output, visualized as a DONE/NEXT split
beats.narration_text: Re-run it, and the shape changes completely. Done this week: the article's published, the video's out in both formats. Starting next week: Suffolk University — a talk with Yatra about Humanitarians AI. Nothing here is finished yet. That's the point of saying so.
beats.visual_intent: Manim: the same three cards, now regrouped under two headers — DONE THIS WEEK (checkmark, good-green) holding the article + video cards; STARTING NEXT WEEK (arrow, terracotta) holding the Suffolk University card — a vertical divider between the two groups

beats.narration_text: So that's the real log: one article shipped, one video actually produced, and one talk still ahead of me. Separating done from next isn't a small detail — it's the difference between a recap and a highlight reel.
beats.visual_intent: recap card: 'done' vs 'next' reframed as the actual lesson, not just a formatting choice
